headline: AstroForge rebounds. SpaceX eyes IPO. True Anomaly raises funds.
deck: This week, AstroForge makes a comeback, while True Anomaly secures significant funding amidst a crowded space market.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has completed a $190 million Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, tapping into increased DoD interest in space safety. This round adds significant firepower to its existing capabilities.
stories.soWhat: In a landscape where cash is king, True Anomaly’s funding is a reminder that security concerns are driving investment more than tech novelty.

stories.head: AstroForge completes DeepSpace-2 spacecraft
stories.body: AstroForge has successfully completed its DeepSpace-2 spacecraft, learning from its previous misadventure. This project aims to mine asteroids, a venture that’s as ambitious as it is risky. The company is reportedly using insights from its past failures to refine its approach.
stories.soWhat: If failures are the best teachers, AstroForge just graduated with honors; expect them to be more cautious yet bold in their next steps.

stories.head: SpaceX plans $75B IPO, stirring market buzz
stories.body: SpaceX is gearing up for an IPO that aims to raise at least $75 billion, a figure that would make it one of the largest tech IPOs in history. Investors are already speculating on the impact this could have on the broader aerospace market and its competitors.
stories.soWhat: A $75 billion IPO could reshape investor sentiment in the space sector, making every launch and contract win feel like a stock tip.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's IPO timeline
watchlist.body: The timing of SpaceX's IPO could influence funding trends across the industry, as investors may rush to capitalize on perceived 'hot' sectors.

watchlist.title: AstroForge's next steps post-DeepSpace-2
watchlist.body: How AstroForge leverages its recent success could set the tone for future asteroid mining endeavors, potentially attracting more venture interest.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris tactical SDA bid
watchlist.body: This partnership could signal a shift in how defense contractors approach space, especially in the realm of satellite defense.

watchlist.title: Watch for True Anomaly's next moves
watchlist.body: With fresh funding, True Anomaly is poised to expand its capabilities, which could disrupt the status quo in co-orbital security.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
